title: Vibe Coding Risks in Business Central. #businesscentral #bc #podcast

quotes.text: those are personal tools, right? They're They're for me. If they break, I'm I'm the only one affected.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why personal vibe-coded tools carry low risk: only the author is affected.

quotes.text: so that's a a limited surface that I'm risk surface I'm exposing myself to.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines the concept of risk surface, the key metric for evaluating the impact of code changes.

quotes.text: since I'm the one who built it, I'm probably also the one who can fix it.
quotes.why_it_matters: The author can also fix the tool, which is part of why personal tools have a limited risk surface.

quotes.text: if I write code a an extension that's used in my business with maybe 200 employees, the the risk surface is a different one.
quotes.why_it_matters: Quantifies the scale difference when extensions are deployed to multiple users, dramatically increasing risk impact.

quotes.text: if it's just like some fancy report, okay, maybe not that critical.
quotes.why_it_matters: Acknowledges that not all extensions have equal risk, with reports being lower risk than core business processes.

quotes.text: if it's uh like touching posting routines or stuff, then maybe you want to be sure that it's not breaking
quotes.why_it_matters: Identifies posting routines as critical processes where code quality and testing are essential in Business Central.
